posts.title: Shakira Sets Amazon Music Livestream Record With Madrid Show and Dua Lipa Duet
posts.excerpt: Shakira's October 3 Madrid concert set a new Amazon Music livestream record for a female artist, with Dua Lipa joining her onstage.
posts.body:
Shakira's October 3 Madrid concert set a new Amazon Music livestream record for a female artist, with Dua Lipa joining her onstage. They performed "Antología," and Amazon announced the record the following day without releasing a viewer total. The performance came during Shakira's Madrid residency.

The concert streamed worldwide through Amazon Music, Prime Video and Twitch, making it Shakira's first complete concert broadcast globally. Amazon's claim is specific to its own platform rather than an all-platform streaming record. The show was also the centerpiece of the 2026 edition of Amazon Music's Women Shaping Latin Music campaign, with a 24-hour replay available after the live broadcast.

Dua Lipa joined Shakira for "Antología," the ballad from *Pies Descalzos*, released in 1995. The Madrid appearance was their first performance together, either onstage or in a studio. The song already had a connection between them. During her 2025 Bogotá stop, Dua Lipa covered "Antología" as part of the local-song tradition she used throughout the *Radical Optimism Tour*. Shakira praised that performance online. The earlier cover had been a solo moment, so the Madrid version turned an online exchange into an actual duet. Organizers considered two songs for the guest appearance and ultimately chose "Antología" for the duet.

[ig:p:DeFRhLolil0|@shakira|https://www.instagram.com/p/DeFRhLolil0/]

The livestream came from Shakira Stadium, the temporary venue built inside Madrid's Iberdrola Music complex for the residency. The stadium holds more than 50,000 people, while Macondo Park extends the project beyond the concert bowl. The site was designed as a temporary city rather than a conventional venue complex.

Inspired by Gabriel García Márquez's fictional Macondo, the project includes eight pavilions devoted to music, fashion, food, literature, art and film, children's culture and Shakira's own career. Workshops, exhibitions and smaller shows run on the same grounds throughout the residency. The setup was conceived as a meeting place for Latin culture, so the audience enters a broader temporary program before and after the main show rather than a stadium with only the concert itself.

posts.title: Frequency Of Love
posts.excerpt: Victoria Monét has released her second album *Frequency Of Love*, a 22-song record that moves between R&B, house, funk and acoustic soul.
posts.body:
Victoria Monét has released her second album *Frequency Of Love*, a 22-song record that moves between R&B, house, funk and acoustic soul. It is her first full-length since *JAGUAR II*, the album that helped turn her into one of the biggest breakthrough stories of the 2024 Grammys.

The long gap was deliberate. After the awards cycle around *JAGUAR II*, she enrolled at the Institute of Culinary Education and graduated in May 2026, then completed an externship at Verse L.A. while rehearsing for Bruno Mars' European stadium tour. Cooking gave her a creative routine with no chart position or campaign attached to it. She described the appeal as "creating something that I wasn't earning from."

At first, *Frequency Of Love* was supposed to lean much harder into yacht rock. Digging through the musicians who worked with Michael Jackson and Quincy Jones led her toward Toto and that late-'70s and early-'80s sound. Culinary school gradually broke open the original plan. Pasta days sent her toward Italian music, and Jamaican dishes sent her toward Jamaican records. By the end, the album no longer belonged to one lane. As she put it, "I don't know that I'll ever be a one-lane person."

"Reach Out" moves into sleek club R&B, "You Hurt Me Too" was written with the drama of a James Bond theme in mind, and "Juicy" carries more of the yacht-rock idea that shaped the album's earliest version. "Reach Out" also predates the finished record. She recorded it around the period when the *JAGUAR II* deluxe edition was being assembled, then held it back because she believed it deserved more than a bonus-track slot. It finally arrived as an advance single for *Frequency Of Love*. The video was filmed at the Salk Institute in La Jolla, where the stark concrete architecture becomes part of the visual rather than a generic performance backdrop.

[youtube:h99lQg2zSl0]

Love on the album is deliberately broader than romance. The songs move through attraction, heartbreak, self-love, motherhood and the risk of trusting someone enough to be hurt. Her daughter Hazel Monét appears alongside Leon Thomas on "You Mean The World To Me." That family moment sits among songs about partners, longing and disappointment rather than in a separate section of the record.

Another thread reaches much further back. "Somebody," written by Harry Warren and Jack Brooks, entered her life when she was a child watching *Introducing Dorothy Dandridge* with her grandmother. Dorothy Dandridge became such a lasting reference that she later dressed as the actress for Halloween twice. The song now sits beside the album's contemporary R&B and dance tracks rather than being treated as a detached retro interlude.

The album now moves into its live chapter. The tour opens October 27 in Raleigh and runs through December 17 in San Francisco. At the same time, the Frequency Of Love Foundation is starting youth programs around food, agriculture, cooking and wellness. Its first projects include hands-on food education and community gardens. The connection to the album is unusually direct. Cooking school changed the music, and now food education is part of what comes next.
